lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 69, which skips the build on PRs with no code and caches the compiler with ccache.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request sixty-nine, which skips the build on pull requests with no code and caches the compiler with see-cache.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A changed-files check, a compiler cache around the build, and a summary that says why build and verify were skipped.
First, the build job lists the files the PR changes on top of main.
If they are all explainers, skills, Markdown or narration files, it marks the run to skip.
Then build and verify skip their heavy steps, but both jobs still finish green.
And the summary comment says they were skipped because no code changed.
When code did change, the job first restores the last compiler cache.
lines.say: When code did change, the job first restores the last compiler cache.

lines.caption: The build runs as before, with every compiler call going through ccache.
lines.say: The build runs as before, with every compiler call going through see-cache.

lines.caption: Then it saves a new cache entry, and GitHub evicts the oldest entries once the repository passes 10 gigabytes.
lines.say: Then it saves a new cache entry, and GitHub evicts the oldest entries once the repository passes ten gigabytes.

lines.caption: Why: Actions ran out of minutes on 7 November, and build and verify billed 541 of them on PRs with no code.
lines.say: Why: Actions ran out of minutes on the seventh of November, and build and verify billed five hundred forty-one of them on pull requests with no code.

lines.caption: Skipping steps rather than whole jobs keeps the checks green.
The check compares GitHub's merge commit with main, so it sees the whole PR, not just the last push.
Anything under debian or verify always builds, even a Markdown file, and so does the packaged README.
In place of the skipped steps, each job runs one step named No code changed.
The summary spots a job that ran the No code changed step, and says the screenshot audit is not needed.
The cache folder is an absolute path, because the Debian build tools give the build a fake home folder.
Each entry is at most 500 megabytes. Old ones are left to GitHub, so the build job needs no extra permission.
lines.say: Each entry is at most five hundred megabytes. Old ones are left to GitHub, so the build job needs no extra permission.

lines.caption: The PR changes the workflow, the summary script and the rules file, and adds this explainer.
To start the compiler cache from cold, or free space by hand, delete its entries under the repository's Actions caches.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built on patterns the workflow already had, checked in the cloud session, then by CI on this PR.
It follows the review's own explainer-only skip, verify's deb cache, and the summary's job states.
The file pattern was run on sample paths: docs were dropped, and code, packaging and CI files kept.
The summary was checked on stand-in jobs and comments, and the workflow file parses.
The skip step was run the way GitHub runs it, and marked a docs-only change to skip.
On CI, the full build and verify passed, and the second build hit the compiler cache 220 times out of 221.
lines.say: On CI, the full build and verify passed, and the second build hit the compiler cache two hundred twenty times out of two hundred twenty-one.

lines.caption: A fresh agent reviewed the diff and found six problems: three were fixed, and two were kept at first.
The main fix: docs-only PRs no longer wait for a screenshot audit when there are no screenshots.
The build job's permission to delete caches was one of those, and CI's review later took it out.
CI's first review found eight. The confirmed one says the merge rule still expects build and verify to run.
The owner chose to change that rule in this PR. The other seven are fixed in one push.
A real docs-only PR, and main's cache seeding new PRs, can only be seen after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later.
The rest of the CI minutes issues follow, in another session, since they edit the same workflow.
Next: fold the small jobs together, edit comments only when they change, and reuse PR debs on main.
That is the PR: docs-only PRs stop building, and every other build reuses the last one's work.
